primary_meaning: To set apart as holy unto God or to make holy (ceremonially, positionally, or progressively) by divine action, especially the Holy Spirit's work conforming believers to Christ

alternatives.meaning: Positional or definitive sanctification: believers are declared holy and set apart once-for-all at conversion through union with Christ
Progressive or experiential sanctification: the ongoing lifelong process of moral and spiritual growth in holiness
Entire or instantaneous sanctification as a second definite work of grace (perfect love or eradication of the sinful nature in this life)
Ritual or ceremonial consecration of objects, places, or persons for sacred use (primarily Old Testament cultic sense)

notes: Core lexical and theological sense of 'make/set apart as holy' is nearly universal across Christian traditions and biblical scholarship; variation concerns timing, extent, and relation to justification rather than the basic meaning itself.
